title: Noor and the Semester
premise: Jude Nakamura, a statistician for the Westfield High swim team, notices the team's win-loss data fits a pattern too perfect to be chance — and then a group chat called 'Semester' starts messaging them predictions that come true within days. The chat is run by students whose parents sit on the school board, and it exists because the board buried a scandal years ago: a pool renovation deal built on falsified safety inspections that endangered athletes, including Jude's late older brother. As Jude decodes the numbers behind the predictions, they must choose between staying invisible — the survival strategy that has kept them safe since their brother's death — or going public with proof that would destroy the found family they've finally built. In the end, Jude testifies at the board hearing with the team standing beside them, exposing the cover-up at the cost of the season being forfeited, but winning something better: a school that tells the truth.
about_author: Jude Ravensworth is the pen name of a former high school math tutor who spent three years listening to teenagers explain how adults fail them. They write quiet, data-obsessed protagonists who discover that numbers can be an act of love.

chapters.title: Head Down, Grades Up
chapters.summary: Jude Nakamura's POV establishes their invisibility strategy: they run stats for the swim team from the bleachers, never in the water, never in photos. A near-miss with a collapsing locker room shelf hints the building itself is failing. Emotional beat: controlled loneliness mistaken for peace.

chapters.title: The Pattern in the Water
chapters.summary: Still Jude's POV. While compiling season statistics, Jude finds win probabilities that defy randomness — meets rescheduled, opponents benched, all tracing back to board-approved facility decisions. They almost tell Coach Reyes, then delete the spreadsheet. Beat: the first flinch of conscience.

chapters.title: Unknown Number
chapters.summary: POV shifts to Priya Chandrasekaran, swim captain, who adds Jude to a group chat called 'Semester' after finding a note in her locker. The chat's first message predicts Friday's fire drill to the minute. It happens exactly. Beat: eerie thrill cracking open routine.

chapters.title: Five Members, One Rule
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. The chat has five members: Priya, Jude, backup goalie Marcus Oyelaran, debate prodigy Sofia Lindqvist, and an anonymous admin called 'Tide.' The rule: no screenshots outside the chat. Marcus wants out; Sofia wants answers. Beat: uneasy alliance forming around shared fear.

chapters.title: What Tide Knows
chapters.summary: Marcus's POV. He traces Tide's IP to a district server and panics — this isn't a prank, it's someone inside the system. Tide posts a second prediction: a star athlete will 'withdraw' before regionals. Beat: dread replacing curiosity as the game turns real.

chapters.title: The Withdrawal
chapters.summary: Sofia's POV. Team star Devon Marsh abruptly transfers, citing 'family reasons,' exactly as predicted. Sofia uses debate skills to press Coach Reyes, who goes pale and stonewalls. Beat: the group realizes someone powerful is feeding Tide information — or cleaning up after them.

chapters.title: Locker Shut
chapters.summary: Back to Jude's POV. Tide DMs Jude directly: 'You already see it. The numbers. Why do you think your brother transferred schools?' Jude shatters — their brother Kai died two years ago at another district school. Beat: grief weaponized; the personal stakes detonate.

chapters.title: Kai's Folder
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Digging through Kai's old files, Jude finds inspection reports for the aquatic center stamped 'passed' on dates the facility was closed. The same inspector signed both districts' documents. Beat: cold clarity — the cover-up spans schools, and Kai was its casualty.

chapters.title: Show Your Work
chapters.summary: Sofia's POV. She organizes the five into roles: Jude runs analysis, Marcus handles tech, Priya manages the team, Sofia builds the argument. Tide sends a partial document — redacted board minutes from the year of the renovation. Beat: purpose crystallizing into a plan.

chapters.title: Regionals, Rigged
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. The team qualifies for regionals on a schedule Tide predicted weeks ago. Priya realizes winning keeps everyone compliant — the season itself is leverage to keep families quiet. Beat: loyalty to the team colliding with loyalty to the truth.

chapters.title: The Leak That Wasn't
chapters.summary: Marcus's POV. Someone leaks a fragment of the group's findings to the student paper, and suspicion falls on Marcus, whose father works for the district. The chat fractures; Sofia accuses him. Beat: betrayal paranoia — the found family's first real crack.

chapters.title: Tide Unmasked
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Cross-referencing Tide's posting times with pool maintenance logs, Jude identifies them: Elena Voss, the aquatic center's young facilities aide, whose mother was the whistleblower fired during the original inspection. Beat: revelation reframing everything — Tide isn't the enemy; she's a survivor recruiting help.

chapters.title: Elena's Testimony
chapters.summary: Elena's POV (first shift away from the five). She explains her mother tried to report falsified inspections, was fired and discredited, and died believing no one would listen. Tide was bait to find students the board couldn't intimidate. Beat: sorrow and fury braided together.

chapters.title: The Offer
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Board member Richard Hale — Devon's uncle — offers Priya a scholarship endorsement if she shuts down the chat and hands over Elena's documents. Priya records the meeting. Beat: temptation made flesh, and the choice that defines her.

chapters.title: Fracture
chapters.summary: Sofia's POV. The recording divides the group: go public now and risk forfeiting regionals, or wait until after the season. Marcus, cleared of suspicion, argues for waiting; Jude, thinking of Kai, cannot. Beat: the found family splits along the fault line of survival versus truth.

chapters.title: What the Water Holds
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Alone at the pool at night, Jude nearly drowns when a corroded vent grate gives way — the exact failure mode Kai's era of inspections should have caught. Elena pulls them out. Beat: the price of silence made physical; no more neutral ground.

chapters.title: Reassembly
chapters.summary: Marcus's POV. The near-drowning ends the debate. Marcus rebuilds trust by securing backups of everything across five devices so no single leak or threat can kill the evidence. The five reunite with Elena. Beat: forgiveness as strategy — the family reforms, stronger for the scar.

chapters.title: Forty-Eight Hours
chapters.summary: Sofia's POV. The board schedules an emergency vote to demolish the aquatic center's records room — legally destroying the originals. The group has two days to file testimony, brief the student paper, and get Coach Reyes on record. Beat: ticking clock at full pressure.

chapters.title: Coach Reyes Decides
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Reyes, who suspected for years but stayed silent to protect his job, chooses to testify, handing over his own hidden copies of maintenance complaints. His confession costs him his coaching license. Beat: an adult choosing consequence over comfort — the theme answered.

chapters.title: The Hearing
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. At the board hearing, Jude presents the statistical case — impossible patterns, matching inspector signatures, the vent failure report — while each friend delivers their piece. Hale attempts to discredit them; Priya plays her recording. Beat: climax — every skill earned across the book deployed at once.

chapters.title: Aftermath, Measured
chapters.summary: Elena's POV. The board resignations begin, the state opens an investigation, and the season is forfeited — the cost the group knew was coming. Devon returns to school. Elena's mother's name is read into the public record. Beat: grief given shape; justice without triumphalism.

chapters.title: Open Water
chapters.summary: Jude's POV, final chapter. Months later, the rebuilt center opens with a plaque for Kai and Elena's mother. Jude swims laps for the first time — head up, breathing easy — and the group chat renames itself 'Family.' Beat: resolution — visibility chosen freely, survival redefined as belonging.
